title: Make room for another person
description: Companionship can be an ordinary expression of care. As you read about the Savior’s attention to individuals, consider who might welcome your time or practical help. This contemporary illustration does not promise that suffering will end on a schedule.

title: Learn from Christ, then practice His teaching
description: This devotional illustration invites attention to Jesus Christ and His disciples. Read His commandment to love one another, then consider how that teaching can shape the way you speak with someone whose beliefs differ from yours.

title: Let a conversation lead to care
description: A meal, an errand or an attentive visit can give a conversation practical meaning. The scene illustrates a present-day application of love; it is not a condition for agreement about belief.

title: Read the invitation to come and know
description: An artistic interpretation of the invitation described in this chapter. Read the account itself for what Christ says and how the people respond. The picture is a study aid, not evidence of a location, garment or historical appearance.

title: Give a passage your attention
description: Read a short passage slowly, consider its setting, and record a question before moving on. This contemporary study illustration accompanies Moroni’s invitation to remember, ponder and ask.

title: Compare the accounts with care
description: Two open books illustrate the practice of comparison. Read each account on its own terms before identifying shared teachings about Jesus Christ. The generated pages are visual texture; use the linked passages for the actual words.

title: Listen to what another reader notices
description: A shared reading can reveal a detail you missed. Let each person name a passage and explain what they noticed before comparing conclusions. This illustration shows an ordinary study conversation.

title: Prepare through learning
description: Bring a specific question to your study of temple worship. Read the dedication prayer’s language about learning, faith and order in context. This desk scene represents preparation rather than a temple ordinance.

title: Connect worship with daily commitments
description: Discuss how promises to God can affect your conduct at home and toward others. Alma’s teaching about baptism offers a passage for considering covenant care; it describes baptism, not a temple ceremony.

title: Keep the record and your interpretation distinct
description: This interpretive writing desk is not Joseph Smith’s actual desk or an original document. As you compare accounts, note who wrote each one, when it was recorded and what question it can help answer.

title: Make room for prayer
description: Luke describes Jesus withdrawing into the wilderness to pray. This devotional interpretation invites a quiet pause before you return to the passage. It does not prescribe a posture or promise a particular feeling.

title: Study, ask and keep a careful record
description: A notebook can help you distinguish the question you brought, what a source says and what you think your next step should be. Read the instruction to study a matter out within its original setting.

title: Let care extend beyond your household
description: This contemporary illustration gives one example of practical help. Read about bearing burdens together and consider a form of service the person receiving it would welcome.

title: Make space for each person’s voice
description: A short shared reading can leave room for different questions, ages and experiences. Consider one teaching you could discuss with a household member, relative or trusted friend.

title: Read the resurrection account
description: An interpretive garden tomb accompanies the scriptural account of the empty tomb. It is not a photograph of an identified historical site. Read what the witnesses encounter and how their understanding develops.

title: Hold hope and remembrance together
description: A conversation about someone who has died can include both sorrow and faith. This contemporary illustration invites patient listening while you consider the scriptural hope of resurrection.

title: Bring the whole storm account into view
description: This devotional interpretation accompanies Mark’s account of Jesus and the disciples on the sea. Notice their question as well as Christ’s response. A miracle in the account should not become a deadline for relief in another person’s life.

title: Take the next step with support
description: Practical companionship can matter while a difficulty continues. Read how the people in Mosiah describe strength while carrying burdens, then consider what support you could seek or offer.

title: Listen without setting a timetable
description: Presence can begin with letting someone speak about the person they miss. This contemporary illustration accompanies the invitation to mourn with those who mourn. Ask what would help, and respect the answer.

title: Leave room for a steady next step
description: Quiet study can be one part of an ordinary day during change. Choose a manageable passage and a question you want to bring to it. This illustration does not imply that spiritual practice replaces practical support.

title: Consider a covenant in practice
description: An ordinary act of help can make a discussion about covenant community concrete. Read the baptismal invitation to bear burdens and consider what thoughtful participation could look like in your own setting.
